title: How Much Does TikTok Pay Creators in 2026?
excerpt: How much TikTok pays creators in 2026: Creator Rewards eligibility and typical payouts, LIVE gifts, subscriptions, TikTok Shop, and why brand deals usually pay more.
content:
How much does TikTok pay?

Quick answer: TikTok pays eligible creators through its Creator Rewards Program for qualified views on videos longer than one minute. TikTok doesn't publish a fixed rate; creators commonly report earning somewhere around $0.40 to $1.00 per 1,000 qualified views, varying by country, niche, watch time and engagement. For most creators, platform payouts are smaller than what they earn from brand deals, UGC and TikTok Shop.

What is the TikTok Creator Rewards Program?

It's TikTok's main program for paying creators directly, replacing the older Creator Fund. It rewards original videos over one minute long, based on qualified views and factors like originality, watch time, search value and audience engagement.

Who can join?

Requirements can change and vary by country, but they have typically included:

  • being at least 18 years old;
  • at least 10,000 followers;
  • at least 100,000 video views in the last 30 days;
  • an account in good standing, in a country where the program is available.

Check the Creator tools section in the TikTok app for current eligibility in your country.

How much is that in practice?

Because the rate is not fixed, use reported ranges only as a rough guide. At around $0.40 to $1.00 per 1,000 qualified views, a video with 100,000 qualified views might earn roughly $40 to $100. Not every view counts as qualified, and payouts vary a lot between creators.

Other ways TikTok pays creators

Income streamHow it works
LIVE giftsViewers send virtual gifts during LIVEs, which convert to rewards you can cash out
SubscriptionsFans pay monthly for perks like badges and subscriber-only content, where available
TikTok Shop affiliateYou earn commission when viewers buy products tagged in your videos
TikTok OneTikTok's marketplace where brands can find and hire creators, where available
Brand deals and UGCBrands pay you directly for videos; not paid by TikTok, but usually the largest income

Why brand deals usually pay more than TikTok

A single brand deal or UGC video can pay more than the platform pays for many thousands of views, and you don't need 10,000 followers to get one. Brands pay for videos that sell their product, so a small creator with good product videos can earn from brands well before qualifying for Creator Rewards. Read how to get brand deals on TikTok.

How to earn more on TikTok

  1. Post consistently in one niche so brands and the algorithm know what you're about.
  2. Make some videos over a minute to qualify for Creator Rewards once eligible.
  3. Tag products you genuinely use through TikTok Shop where available.
  4. Pitch brands every week for paid videos and UGC, and follow up.

faq.question: How much does TikTok pay per 1,000 views?
faq.answer: TikTok doesn't publish a fixed rate. Creators in the Creator Rewards Program commonly report roughly $0.40 to $1.00 per 1,000 qualified views, depending on country, niche, watch time and engagement.

faq.question: How many followers do you need to get paid on TikTok?
faq.answer: The Creator Rewards Program has typically required at least 10,000 followers and 100,000 views in the last 30 days, plus being 18 or older in an eligible country. Brand deals and UGC have no follower minimum.

faq.question: How much does TikTok pay for 1 million views?
faq.answer: At commonly reported rates of about $0.40 to $1.00 per 1,000 qualified views, 1 million qualified views could earn roughly $400 to $1,000 through Creator Rewards, but actual payouts vary and not every view qualifies.

faq.question: Does TikTok still have the Creator Fund?
faq.answer: No. TikTok replaced the Creator Fund with the Creator Rewards Program, which focuses on original videos longer than one minute.

faq.question: What pays more, TikTok or brand deals?
faq.answer: For most creators, brand deals and UGC pay more than platform payouts. One paid video for a brand can be worth more than the platform pays for a large number of views.
